sentences: Under a wide sky, people gather on the sand.
Women in full, billowing skirts and gentlemen take the sea air, and among them we can find dogs, horses and carriages.
This is On the Beach at Trouville, painted in 1863 by the French artist Eugène Boudin.
It is painted in oil on a wooden panel, small and wide, 26.
7 centimetres high and 48.
3 centimetres across.
It came to The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York in 1907 as a bequest from Amelia B.
Lazarus. Follow the figures slowly from the left.
The women's skirts swell out in round domes.
This is the crinoline, a framework of hoops worn under the skirt.
The fashion of 1860s Paris has simply moved to the seashore.
Now move toward the right.
Among the people are dogs, horses and carriages.
Hardly anyone is in the water.
Everyone is fully dressed, strolling on the sand or standing to talk.
Why was this scene new?
Seaside resorts such as Trouville and Deauville were only just coming into being, as villas and hotels went up along the Normandy coast for visitors from the cities.
Boudin started painting these beaches around 1862.
At the time, it was a strikingly modern subject.
Now look up at the sky.
Boudin devoted his life to painting skies, clouds and the air of the coast.
The painter Camille Corot is said to have called him the king of skies.
Look at the brushwork too.
Faces and folds of cloth are not carefully drawn.
The colour is laid on quickly and lightly.
Boudin called nature his great master and tried to keep his first impression intact, and critics complained that his pictures looked like an unfinished sketch.
Boudin was born in 1824 in Honfleur, into a family of sailors.
He opened a shop in Le Havre selling paper, paints and frames to visiting artists, and it was there that he turned to painting himself.
Back in Normandy he met the young Claude Monet and persuaded him to try painting in oil outdoors.
Monet later said that he owed becoming a painter to Boudin.
Boudin also took part in the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.
Step back and take it in.
On a panel barely the size of two hands lie the wind, the light and a brand-new kind of leisure.
Today, take a moment to look up at the sky outside your window.
